annotations.text:
SensorLab — free-fall lab, measuring g.
One system, two modes. Steps 2, 3 and 5 are PEDAGOGICAL mode: warm off-white, generous. Step 4 is INSTRUMENT mode: dark, dense, credible. The switch is the cue — going dark means you are taking a real measurement.
Chrome stays ink-black on purpose, so amber and cyan only ever carry meaning.

INSTRUMENT MODE
Dark, tabular numerals, a rolling trace, and the trigger threshold drawn on the chart. Axis runs to 30 m/s² so the impact spike it is armed for cannot clip off the top.
Haptic and tone on trigger, because during a free-fall lab nobody is looking at the screen.

THE COLOUR LANGUAGE
Prediction = warm amber, DASHED.
Measured reality = cool cyan, SOLID.
Separated by dash pattern as well as hue — the comparison is the product, and colour alone fails ~8% of viewers.
Here it carries the lesson too: the sketch grew, the measurement went to zero.

BILINGUAL / RTL
The chrome mirrors: chevron flips and moves right, the rail fills from the right, text right-aligns, the language pill swaps its active side.
The DATA does not. Axes still run left-to-right, numerals stay Latin, the formula stays LTR. Only the words inside the plot are translated.
